article_3__section_021__chunk_001.article_summary: This survey investigates how user perceptions, personal norms, and social influences shape intentions to use smart home technologies specifically for improving household energy efficiency. It combines the theory of planned behavior and the norm activation model, showing that personal moral norms, sense of responsibility, and awareness of environmental consequences are the strongest predictors of energy-efficient smart home use. The authors propose that smart home systems should reinforce pro-environmental norms, support habit formation, and provide personalized feedback on environmental and financial outcomes to encourage sustained efficient use. They further suggest embedding green automation defaults and policy incentives that reward household energy savings as design levers to unlock the technology’s full energy-saving potential.

article_5__section_001__chunk_001.green_categories: lighting_efficiency, occupancy_based_control, hvac_optimization, appliance_energy_management, environmental_awareness, scheduling_optimization, standby_reduction
article_5__section_001__chunk_001.article_summary: This paper reports two online surveys (general end users and experienced amateur automators) investigating attitudes, practices, and needs about smart-home automations with a focus on environmental sustainability; respondents show clear interest in monitoring energy consumption, receiving recommendations for optimal appliance activation times, and tools to identify excessive consumption. Experienced users report concrete energy-focused automations: HVAC scheduling tied to occupancy and windows, lighting and appliance shutoff based on presence, load management to avoid meter overload, and synchronizing device operation with photovoltaic production; both groups request better UX, integration/standardization, and AI-assisted suggestions to support greener behavior. The authors conclude that sustainable-management features (monitoring, recommendation, conflict detection) and improved end-user development interfaces are needed to make green automations accessible to more users.

article_5__section_007__chunk_001.article_summary: This paper reports two online surveys (general end users and experienced amateur automators) investigating attitudes, practices, and needs about smart-home automations with a focus on environmental sustainability; respondents show clear interest in monitoring energy consumption, receiving recommendations for optimal appliance activation times, and tools to identify excessive consumption. Experienced users report concrete energy-focused automations: HVAC scheduling tied to occupancy and windows, lighting and appliance shutoff based on presence, load management to avoid meter overload, and synchronizing device operation with photovoltaic production; both groups request better UX, integration/standardization, and AI-assisted suggestions to support greener behavior. The authors conclude that sustainable-management features (monitoring, recommendation, conflict detection) and improved end-user development interfaces are needed to make green automations accessible to more users.

article_6__section_001__chunk_001.source_title: The role of environmental awareness, renewable energy, and green innovation in shaping climate change perceptions
article_6__section_001__chunk_001.header_path: The role of environmental awareness, renewable energy, and green innovation in shaping climate change perceptions > Abstract
article_6__section_001__chunk_001.article_summary: This article studies how environmental awareness, renewable energy adoption, and green innovation adoption interact within Chinese SMEs and uses the Value–Belief–Norm (VBN) framework to explain how awareness translates into pro-environmental practices; it treats renewable energy adoption as a mediator and green innovation as a moderator influencing perceptions of climate change severity. The paper discusses practical levers (policy, managerial actions, and incentives) that encourage renewable energy and green innovations, highlights potential behavioral effects (e.g., reduced perceived severity due to perceived efficacy), and emphasizes raising awareness to drive concrete sustainability actions. Methods and measures (survey items, PLS-SEM analysis) are described for assessing relationships among awareness, adoption of renewables/innovations, and perceived climate risk, which could inform design choices and evaluation metrics for greener smart-home automations that aim to change user behavior or adopt cleaner technologies.
